experiment: P5k GPU-compute-guarded shared frozen-forward and dense bounded-head execution
research_question: Can the unchanged P5g one-forward dense-head execution preserve exact frozen P5e outputs while reducing CUDA-synchronized end-to-end latency when cost isolation is enforced by rejecting only external Python processes with an actual CUDA compute context?
single_changed_axis: No scientific mechanism changes from P5g. P5k changes only fresh identities and refines the cost guard from external Python process presence to external Python CUDA-compute PID presence, validated by nvidia-smi pmon.

execution.reference: two frozen base forwards plus unchanged dense attachment
execution.candidate: one frozen base forward plus identical unchanged dense attachment
execution.timing: CUDA synchronize before and after each run; before and after every warmup/repeat reject any external Python PID whose nvidia-smi pmon process type contains C; record CPU-only Python PIDs and GPU snapshot

development_data.roles: evaluation-only; no training, selection, calibration or threshold adjustment

stop_rule: Any exception or external Python CUDA-compute PID at a guard checkpoint freezes accessed P5k identities without result. Any equivalence or latency failure stops P5k with no threshold, head, weight, feature, batch, scheduling, compiler or quantization change and no confirmation.

confirmation_if_and_only_if_development_.decision: Only a pass supports a narrow frozen-execution cost claim, never a new architecture or classification claim.
